title: Identity handles merge into one customer and an ambiguous merge fails closed
risk: Two handles belonging to one person stay split, or two different people are merged, so orders, consent and conversations attach to the wrong human. Blueprint is silent on merge-conflict arbitration, so this is an extension probe with a proposed configuration, not an SRS requirement.
preconditions: Tenant T1 with cust-a owning handles wa_id_a and cust-a@example.invalid in run namespace run-t1-merge-*
A second unlinked handle cust-a2@example.invalid observed in the same session history

merge_request.evidence: exact email confirmation in verified session

steps.action: Merge the incoming handle that carries exact-verification evidence into cust-a
steps.expected: the handle joins cust-a, one customer identity row exists, and prior orders/timeline/consent of cust-a stay intact

steps.action: Attempt the conflicting merge that is supported only by a device fingerprint
steps.expected: the merge is refused as unverified, no identity row moves and the attempt is recorded

steps.action: Re-run the accepted merge with the identical request identity
steps.expected: the operation is idempotent: still exactly one identity row and one merge audit entry

steps.action: Read the customer projection for cust-a and for cust-b after both attempts
steps.expected: cust-a shows the merged handle, cust-b keeps exactly its own handle, and no conversation or order moved between them

assertions: After the accepted merge the identity table holds exactly one row per (tenant, channel_type, identifier) and cust-a owns 3 handles
The fingerprint-only merge is refused and cust-b retains exactly 1 handle with its own orders
No order, conversation or consent record changed owner during either attempt
forbidden: Silently union two independently verified accounts into one customer
Move a consent record between customers during a merge
evidence: Identity rows for cust-a and cust-b after each attempt with their channel identifiers
Merge audit entries for the accepted and the refused attempt
cleanup: Unlink and delete the run-scoped merged handle row for run-t1-merge-*; retain both audit entries
automation: Drive the real identity service with fixture handles; device-fingerprint evidence is intentionally insufficient. Blueprint-silent arbitration rules are declared here as proposed configuration and must not be reported as SRS behavior.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
